titleStmt.title: Three groups of interneurons account for nearly 100% of neocortical GABAergic neurons
titleStmt.author: Rudy
Fishell
Lee
Hjerling-Leffler

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Three groups of interneurons account for nearly 100% of neocortical GABAergic neurons

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether the diversity of neocortical inhibitory interneurons can be exhaustively partitioned by three molecular markers
span.quote: This analysis has provided strong evidence that three major groups of neurons, those expressing the Ca 2+ -binding protein parvalbumin (PV), those expressing the neuropeptide somatostatin (SST), and those expressing 5HT3aRs account for nearly 100% of GABAergic neurons in somatosensory (S1) cortex.

span.label: parvalbumin, somatostatin and 5HT3a receptor expression together account for nearly 100 percent of GABAergic interneurons in somatosensory cortex
span.quote: This analysis revealed that 5HT3aR neurons account for ~30% of the total population of GABAergic neurons, and that three group of neurons, those expressing PV, SST, and 5HT3aR, account for nearly all, if not all, GABAergic interneurons in primary somatosensory cortex

span.label: existence
span.quote: This analysis has provided strong evidence that three major groups of neurons, those expressing the Ca 2+ -binding protein parvalbumin (PV), those expressing the neuropeptide somatostatin (SST), and those expressing 5HT3aRs account for nearly 100% of GABAergic neurons in somatosensory (S1) cortex.

span.label: neocortical GABAergic interneuron diversity
span.quote: An understanding of the diversity of cortical GABAergic interneurons is critical to understand the function of the cerebral cortex.

span.label: review
span.quote: It is largely based on the analysis of a population of GABAergic interneurons in mouse neocortex that express the ionotropic serotonin receptor 5HT3a (5HT3aR).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: excitatory synapses onto Martinotti cells facilitate, so sustained firing of a single pyramidal cell builds up enough drive to make the Martinotti cell fire and inhibit pyramidal cells across layers and columns
span.quote: As a result of this feature, repetitive activity in a single pyramidal cell can drive a Martinotti cell to fire and provide feedback inhibition to pyramidal neurons across layers and columns ( Kapfer et al., 2007 ; Silberberg and Markram, 2007 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: because those inputs facilitate, the strength of Martinotti-mediated feedback inhibition grows with the rate and duration of presynaptic discharge
span.quote: Given the facilitating dynamics of Martinotti cell excitatory inputs, the feedback inhibition mediated by these neurons will increase as a function of rate and duration of presynaptic discharge.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the delay between thalamocortical excitation of pyramidal cells and disynaptic inhibition from FS cells opens a brief integration window that limits temporal summation
span.quote: The latency between the onset of the TC excitation of excitatory cells and the onset of feedforward inhibition from FS cells results in a brief time window during which the excitatory neurons can integrate TC inputs.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: ionotropic serotonin and acetylcholine receptors let neuromodulatory systems recruit 5HT3aR interneurons fast enough to be gated by brain state and behavioral context
span.quote: Perhaps, neuromodulatory systems rapidly engage these INs during specific brain states and behavioral contexts that are linked to these neuromodulators.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a locally different chloride concentration at the axon initial segment shifts the GABA-A reversal potential, so chandelier-cell GABA release depolarizes rather than inhibits the pyramidal cell
span.quote: It was recently shown that postsynaptic responses to GABA release from these neurons are depolarizing because of changes in Cl − concentration, and hence the reversal potential of GABA A receptors, at the pyramidal cell AIS, the target of chandelier cell axons, and may in fact be excitatory ( Szabadics et al., 2006 ; Woodruff et al., 2009 ; but see Glickfeld et al., 2009 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: neurogliaform axonal varicosities lacking classical synaptic contacts still hyperpolarize neighbours, implying GABA acts by volume release into the extracellular space
span.quote: These results led to the suggestion that neurogliaform cells influence target neurons by volume release of GABA ( Olah et al., 2009 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the low input resistance of X94 SST cells prevents a single excitatory cell from driving them unless a muscarinic agonist raises their excitability
span.quote: As a result of their lower input resistance, X94 cells are usually not driven to fire by repetitive activity in a single excitatory cell; however, the cells can be excited if the excitatory input is delivered in the presence of a muscarinic agonist (Xu and Rudy, unpublished observations).

span.label: fast-spiking basket cells fire sustained high-frequency trains with the lowest input resistance and fastest membrane time constant of all interneurons, which is what makes their inhibition fast
span.quote: FS cells fire sustained high-frequency trains of brief APs with a large and fast AHP and with little spike frequency adaptation. Near threshold, they fire abrupt episodes of nonadapting repetitive discharges. They have the lowest input resistance and the fastest membrane time constant of all interneurons, a feature that contributes to ensure fast synaptic responses

span.label: excitatory synapses onto fast-spiking cells depress while those onto Martinotti cells facilitate, which is the key functional difference between the two groups
span.quote: Excitatory inputs onto Martinotti cells are generally strongly facilitating, which is a key feature that distinguishes these interneurons from FS neurons

span.label: because of that facilitation, repetitive firing of a single pyramidal cell can drive a Martinotti cell and produce feedback inhibition across layers and columns
span.quote: As a result of this feature, repetitive activity in a single pyramidal cell can drive a Martinotti cell to fire and provide feedback inhibition to pyramidal neurons across layers and columns

span.label: the two groups may therefore be recruited at opposite ends of network activity, one when activity is high and the other transiently when it is low
span.quote: These interneurons might be activated preferentially during periods of increased network activity in contrast to FS cells, which might be transiently activated preferentially when network activity is low.

span.label: 5HT3aR interneurons are heterogeneous but all are potently modulated by ionotropic serotonin receptors, and no response was seen in PV or SST cells
span.quote: Although 5HT3aR interneurons are heterogeneous, they are all potently modulated by ionotropic serotonin receptors ( Lee et al., 2010 ). Local somatic application of mCPBG, a 5HT3aR-selective agonist, to EGFP-positive neurons evoked fast and robust depolarization in more than 40 cells tested throughout all layers and including all the subtypes identified electrophysiologically. In contrast, no response was observed after application of mCPBG to PV and SST-expressing neurons.

span.label: neurogliaform cells may act by volume release of GABA rather than through classical synaptic contacts
span.quote: It was recently observed that neurogliaform axonal varicosities containing synaptic vesicles were often not associated with classical synaptic contacts, although neurogliaform cells produced hyperpolarizing responses in a large fraction of neighboring neurons. These results led to the suggestion that neurogliaform cells influence target neurons by volume release of GABA

span.label: Subtype frequencies within the three groups cannot be estimated because specific markers are lacking.
span.note: what this limits: any quantitative claim about subtypes within the three groups: THE LACK OF SPECIFIC MARKERS MAKES IT DIFFICULT TO ESTIMATE THE FREQUENCIES OF EACH OF THE SUBTYPES
span.quote: The lack of specific markers makes it difficult to estimate the frequencies of each of the subtypes described above.

span.label: The random sample from the 5HT3aR mouse is still too small to fix subtype proportions.
span.note: what this limits: the subtype proportions specifically: THE SAMPLE IS NOT YET SUFFICIENTLY LARGE TO DEFINITELY ESTABLISH SUBTYPE PROPORTIONS
span.quote: Although these studies have been performed by sampling randomly in the 5HT3aR mouse, the sample is not yet sufficiently large to definitely establish subtype proportions from the frequency of observing particular firing patterns.

span.label: The exhaustive-partition conclusion is established mainly for one cortical area, S1.
span.note: what this limits: the scope of the exhaustive-partition claim itself: the conclusion that these neurons ACCOUNT FOR nearly all remaining interneurons rests mainly on S1, not on neocortex at large
span.quote: The availability of a mouse line expressing EGFP in all neocortical 5HT3aR-expressing neurons and without ectopic expression allowed Lee et al. (2010) to conclude that these neurons account for virtually all the interneurons that do not express PV or SST, at least within S1 cortex, where the majority of the analysis has been done so far.

span.label: Output connectivity and function of the 5HT3aR group are largely unknown apart from neurogliaform cells.
span.note: what this limits: any functional or circuit claim about the 5HT3aR group: OTHER THAN NEUROGLIAFORM CELLS, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE OUTPUT CONNECTIONS AND FUNCTION OF 5HT3AR INTERNEURONS
span.quote: Furthermore, other than neurogliaform cells, little is known about the output connections and function of 5HT3aR interneurons.

span.label: The size of any preoptic-area contribution to the 5HT3aR population is unresolved.
span.note: what this limits: the developmental-origin account: IT REMAINS TO BE SHOWN DIRECTLY WHETHER THE NKX5-1 CRE LABELED NEURONS EXPRESS 5HT3AR, and the size of the POA contribution is undetermined
span.quote: It remains to be shown directly whether the Nkx5-1 cre labeled neurons express 5HT3aR and to determine the size of the POA contribution to the 5HT3aR population.

span.label: subtype frequencies within the three groups cannot be estimated for want of specific markers, and the samples are not large enough to settle proportions from firing patterns
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as items 0 and 1 - subtype frequencies, not the three-group partition
span.quote: The lack of specific markers makes it difficult to estimate the frequencies of each of the subtypes described above. Although these studies have been performed by sampling randomly in the 5HT3aR mouse, the sample is not yet sufficiently large to definitely establish subtype proportions from the frequency of observing particular firing patterns.

span.label: the correspondence between subtypes described by different investigators is not easy to establish, which the authors say calls for better classification tools
span.note: what this limits: any attempt to read this classification against another lab's: THE CORRESPONDENCE BETWEEN THE SUBTYPES ... IS NOT EASY TO ESTABLISH - the categories do not map across investigators
span.quote: Furthermore, the correspondence between the subtypes of neurons studied by Xu and Callaway and the subtypes of 5HT3aR neurons described by other investigators is not easy to establish, emphasizing the need to develop better tools to classify 5HT3aR neurons.

span.label: outside neurogliaform cells, little is known about the outputs or function of the 5HT3aR group, which is less understood than the other two
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 3 - outputs and function of the 5HT3aR group
span.quote: Furthermore, other than neurogliaform cells, little is known about the output connections and function of 5HT3aR interneurons. Overall, these cells are more poorly understood than PV and SST interneurons.

span.label: the preponderance of this class of PV neurons is not known and it has not been described by other investigators, perhaps because Blatow et al. used 14-day-old mice and recorded at room temperature
span.note: what this limits: the PV class in question, whose existence may be an age effect: THE PREPONDERANCE OF THIS CLASS OF PV NEURONS IS NOT KNOWN AND HAS NOT BEEN DESCRIBED BY OTHER INVESTIGATORS; PERHAPS BECAUSE BLATOW ET AL. USED 14-DAY-OLD MICE, SOMEWHAT YOUNGER THAN WHAT IS TYPICALLY USED IN THE FIELD
span.quote: The preponderance of this class of PV neurons is not known and has not been described by other investigators; perhaps because Blatow et al. used 14-day-old mice, somewhat younger than what is typically used in the field and carried their recordings at room temperature.

span.label: two extra SST subtypes reported in one study were not seen by others using the same mouse line, and immaturity at the ages used is offered as an explanation
span.note: what this limits: the two additional SST groups: SEVERAL INVESTIGATORS HAVE USED THE GIN LINE TO STUDY MARTINOTTI CELLS AND HAVE NOT REPORTED THE TWO OTHER GROUPS OF SST NEURONS DESCRIBED BY MCGARRY ET AL.
span.quote: Several investigators have used the GIN line to study Martinotti cells and have not reported the two other groups of SST neurons described by McGarry et al. ( Ma et al., 2006 ; Xu et al., 2006 ; Fanselow et al., 2008 ; Xu and Callaway, 2009 ). McGarry et al. (2010) used mice with an average age of P14 (range P10–18), which is younger than what other investigators have used. FS cells mature significantly during an equivalent developmental period showing underdeveloped processes at early ages ( Okaty et al., 2009 ; Goldberg et al., 2010 ). Some of the diversity observed in the study by McGarry et al. (2010) may reflect the presence of immature neurons.

span.label: a bacterial artificial chromosome reporter line used to make an uncountable population countable
span.quote: There are no antibodies to the 5HT3a receptor available, precluding the use of IHC to determine the size of the 5HT3aR-expressing interneuron population and estimate its contribution to the total interneuron family. The availability of a GFP mouse line that reliably reports the presence of 5HT3a receptors allowed us to characterize this interneuron population

span.label: derivation from different areas during development, offered as a feature arguing for a true delineation between two marker-defined Martinotti subtypes
span.quote: Another feature arguing for a true delineation between SOM+/CR− and SOM+/CR+ Martinotti cells is evidence suggesting that they are derived from different areas during development, with the SOM+/CR+ population mainly arising from the dorsal Nkx6-2-positive region of the MGE

span.label: THE PARTITION DEPENDS ON THE ASSAY: PV and SST are non-overlapping by protein immunofluorescence, but under in situ hybridisation up to 16.3 percent of PV cells in layer VI carry SST mRNA, and by RT-PCR a large percentage do
span.quote: We do find that using in situ hybridization (ISH) some PV-containing neurons (<10%) in somatosensory cortex contain SST mRNA. The overlap is largest in layer VI where ~16.3% of PV cells express SST mRNA ( Lee et al., 2010 ). Furthermore, RT-PCR of FACS purified PV-expressing neurons shows SST mRNA expression in a large percentage of the samples

span.label: and the conflict is resolved by CHOOSING the assay: protein expression is taken to define the two groups, with the mRNA overlap explained as levels too low to detect
span.quote: Together, the data suggest that although a fraction of PV neurons may express SST mRNA transcripts, SST protein levels are absent or are too low to be detected by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Thus, the data support the view that PV and SST protein expression defines two independent groups of GABAergic interneurons.

span.label: the 5HT3aR class could not be counted before the tool existed - there are no antibodies to the receptor, so the group had no size until a BAC transgenic line reported it
span.quote: There are no antibodies to the 5HT3a receptor available, precluding the use of IHC to determine the size of the 5HT3aR-expressing interneuron population and estimate its contribution to the total interneuron family. The availability of a GFP mouse line that reliably reports the presence of 5HT3a receptors allowed us to characterize this interneuron population

span.label: the reporter line was validated in both directions: no cell carried EGFP without the transcript, and 99.8 percent of receptor-expressing cells carried EGFP
span.quote: Using the GENSAT line, Lee et al. (2010) found a nearly perfect overlap between EGFP and 5HT3a receptor mRNA expression in the neocortex. There were no false positives, no neuron expressed EGFP that did not also contain 5HT3aR mRNA transcripts. Conversely, there were virtually no false negatives because 99.8 ± 0.3% of neocortical cells expressing the receptor were EGFP positive.

span.label: ONE CELL TYPE, FOUR NAMES, IN ONE SENTENCE: regular adapting nonpyramidal, burst spiking nonpyramidal, intrinsic bursting and low-threshold spike all denote the same Martinotti cells
span.quote: They display a regular adapting firing pattern (RSNP), but often, particularly in layer V, they initially fire bursts of two or more spikes on slow depolarizing humps when depolarized from hyperpolarized potentials (because of this property, these cells have also been called burst spiking nonpyramidal (BSNP), intrinsic bursting (IB), or low-threshold spike (LTS) cells).

span.label: the claim runs one way only: virtually all PV cells are fast-spiking, which does NOT entail that fast-spiking cells are PV
span.quote: PV expression has been associated with the fast-spiking firing pattern since the 1980s ( Kawaguchi et al., 1987 ). This correlation between fast spiking and PV expression has been confirmed by many laboratories ( Cauli et al., 1997 ; Kawaguchi and Kubota, 1997 ; Gibson et al., 1999 ; Ascoli et al., 2008 ; Xu and Callaway, 2009 ), including our own. We have recorded from several hundred PV-expressing neurons in several mouse lines expressing GFP in PV neurons and virtually all are fast-spiking.

span.label: method: review
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: review — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: This analysis has provided strong evidence that three major groups of neurons, those expressing the Ca 2+ -binding protein parvalbumin (PV), those expressing the neuropeptide somatostatin (SST), and those expressing 5HT3aRs account for nearly 100% of GABAergic neurons in somatosensory (S1) cortex.

span.label: phenomenon: a cortical interneuron population that had resisted exhaustive classification
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: neocortical GABAergic interneuron diversity — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Although further work is necessary to characterize in detail the PV, SST, and 5HT3aR neuronal groups, it is already clear that they are heterogenous, each consisting of more than one interneuron class. Of these, the 5HT3aR group might be particularly heterogenous. The challenge to understand interneuron diversity in neocortex now is in understanding the diversity within each of these three groups

span.label: builds-on → Lee et al. (2010)
span.quote: The availability of a GFP mouse line that reliably reports the presence of 5HT3a receptors allowed us to characterize this interneuron population ( Lee et al., 2010 ).

span.label: replicates → Gonchar and Burkhalter (1997); Kawaguchi and Kubota (1997); Ascoli et al. (2008) - PV and SST as non-overlapping interneuron markers
span.quote: Our own studies in mouse have confirmed this conclusion; neurons expressing PV (as detected by immunofluorescence) do not express SST protein and vice versa ( Lee et al., 2010 ).

span.label: contradicts → McGarry et al. (2010) report of two additional SST subtypes in GIN mice
span.quote: Some of the diversity observed in the study by McGarry et al. (2010) may reflect the presence of immature neurons.

span.label: extends → the use of calcium-binding proteins and neuropeptides as markers distinguishing cortical interneurons
span.quote: The conclusion that PV-, SST-, and 5HT3aR-expressing neurons account for nearly if not all GABAergic interneurons in mouse somatosensory cortex implies that other interneuron markers such as the neuropeptides VIP, NPY, and cholecystokinin (CCK) and the Ca 2+ -binding proteins calretinin and calbindin either label small interneuron populations or are expressed in one or more of the three groups defined above.

span.label: critiques → the treatment of VIP, NPY, cholecystokinin, calretinin and calbindin as markers of independent interneuron classes
span.quote: The conclusion that PV-, SST-, and 5HT3aR-expressing neurons account for nearly if not all GABAergic interneurons in mouse somatosensory cortex implies that other interneuron markers such as the neuropeptides VIP, NPY, and cholecystokinin (CCK) and the Ca 2+ -binding proteins calretinin and calbindin either label small interneuron populations or are expressed in one or more of the three groups defined above.

span.label: builds-on → Lee 2010's double in situ hybridisation quantification of the three marker populations
span.quote: This analysis revealed that 5HT3aR neurons account for ~30% of the total population of GABAergic neurons, and that three group of neurons, those expressing PV, SST, and 5HT3aR, account for nearly all, if not all, GABAergic interneurons in primary somatosensory cortex

span.label: qualifies → the view that parvalbumin cells are the largest interneuron class
span.quote: 5HT3aR interneurons primarily populate superficial neocortical layers I–III ( Fig. 1 ). In fact, these cells are the predominant population of interneurons (~60% of all interneurons) in these layers. Within layers I–III, the number of 5HT3aR-expressing neurons actually exceeds by two fold the number of PV-positive neurons, traditionally believed to represent the largest interneuron class.

span.label: PV —distinct-from→ SST
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — BY PROTEIN. The same two groups OVERLAP by mRNA, so this edge is only true relative to the assay named in it
span.quote: Our own studies in mouse have confirmed this conclusion; neurons expressing PV (as detected by immunofluorescence) do not express SST protein and vice versa

span.label: PV —contrasted-with→ ISH
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — THE PARTITION DEPENDS ON THE ASSAY: under 10 percent of PV cells carry SST mRNA overall, 16.3 percent in layer VI, and a large percentage by RT-PCR
span.quote: We do find that using in situ hybridization (ISH) some PV-containing neurons (<10%) in somatosensory cortex contain SST mRNA. The overlap is largest in layer VI where ~16.3% of PV cells express SST mRNA ( Lee et al., 2010 ). Furthermore, RT-PCR of FACS purified PV-expressing neurons shows SST mRNA expression in a large percentage of the samples

span.label: IHC —operationalised-as→ SST
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — THE CONFLICT RESOLVED BY CHOOSING: PROTEIN expression is taken as definitional and the mRNA overlap explained as levels too low for immunohistochemistry to see
span.quote: Together, the data suggest that although a fraction of PV neurons may express SST mRNA transcripts, SST protein levels are absent or are too low to be detected by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Thus, the data support the view that PV and SST protein expression defines two independent groups of GABAergic interneurons.

span.label: 5HT3aR —part-of→ GABAergic
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the third of three groups that together account for nearly all of them
span.quote: This analysis revealed that 5HT3aR neurons account for ~30% of the total population of GABAergic neurons, and that three group of neurons, those expressing PV, SST, and 5HT3aR, account for nearly all, if not all, GABAergic interneurons in primary somatosensory cortex

span.label: PV —part-of→ GABAergic
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — one of the three groups whose union is claimed to be the whole population
span.quote: This analysis revealed that 5HT3aR neurons account for ~30% of the total population of GABAergic neurons, and that three group of neurons, those expressing PV, SST, and 5HT3aR, account for nearly all, if not all, GABAergic interneurons in primary somatosensory cortex

span.label: EGFP —operationalised-as→ 5HT3aR
span.note: status: ATTRIBUTED TO A NAMED STUDY, IN A REVIEW: 'Using the GENSAT line, LEE ET AL. (2010) FOUND a nearly perfect overlap between EGFP and 5HT3a receptor mRNA expression in the neocortex.' The overlap is Lee et al.'s measurement and the reporting is this review's, which is what a review does. · strength of the relation: 1 — VALIDATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: no false positives at all, and 99.8 percent of receptor-expressing cells were reporter-positive
span.quote: Using the GENSAT line, Lee et al. (2010) found a nearly perfect overlap between EGFP and 5HT3a receptor mRNA expression in the neocortex. There were no false positives, no neuron expressed EGFP that did not also contain 5HT3aR mRNA transcripts. Conversely, there were virtually no false negatives because 99.8 ± 0.3% of neocortical cells expressing the receptor were EGFP positive.

span.label: 5HT3aR —distinct-from→ IHC
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — A CATEGORY THAT NEEDED A TOOL TO EXIST: no antibodies to the receptor, so this population had no measurable size until a reporter line was made
span.quote: There are no antibodies to the 5HT3a receptor available, precluding the use of IHC to determine the size of the 5HT3aR-expressing interneuron population and estimate its contribution to the total interneuron family. The availability of a GFP mouse line that reliably reports the presence of 5HT3a receptors allowed us to characterize this interneuron population

span.label: PV —operationalised-as→ fast-spiking
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — ONE DIRECTION ONLY: virtually all PV cells are fast-spiking. It does NOT follow that fast-spiking cells are PV - see Moore2013, where up to 40 percent of PV-negative cells would be called fast-spiking
span.quote: PV expression has been associated with the fast-spiking firing pattern since the 1980s ( Kawaguchi et al., 1987 ). This correlation between fast spiking and PV expression has been confirmed by many laboratories ( Cauli et al., 1997 ; Kawaguchi and Kubota, 1997 ; Gibson et al., 1999 ; Ascoli et al., 2008 ; Xu and Callaway, 2009 ), including our own. We have recorded from several hundred PV-expressing neurons in several mouse lines expressing GFP in PV neurons and virtually all are fast-spiking.

span.label: basket cells —part-of→ PV
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: There are two types of PV neurons: basket cells, neurons that make synapses at the soma and proximal dendrite of target neurons and typically have multipolar morphology, and chandelier cells, which target the axon initial segment (AIS) of pyramidal cells

span.label: chandelier cells —part-of→ PV
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: There are two types of PV neurons: basket cells, neurons that make synapses at the soma and proximal dendrite of target neurons and typically have multipolar morphology, and chandelier cells, which target the axon initial segment (AIS) of pyramidal cells

span.label: Martinotti cells —part-of→ SST
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: SST expression in neocortex has typically been associated with Martinotti cells (MCs), GABAergic interneurons with ascending axons that arborize in layer I spreading horizontally to neighboring columns and making synapses on the dendritic tufts of pyramidal neurons.

span.label: X94 —operationalised-as→ input resistance
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — a second SST type separated from Martinotti cells partly by a property that makes it resemble PV cells instead
span.quote: X94 cells in S1 cortex were located in layer IV and V and had axonal projections that instead of reaching and targeting layer I, innervate profusely layer IV. The cells also differed from Martinotti cells in a number of electrophysiological properties. X94 cells had a much lower input resistance, approaching that of FS cells. They had spikes of shorter duration and often produced a stuttering firing pattern. They were capable of firing at higher frequencies than Martinotti cells but, in contrast to FS neurons, exhibited spike frequency adaptation

span.label: facilitating —contrasted-with→ depressing
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: the synaptic dynamics of the INPUTS, not the cell itself - and even that has a layer VI exception the paper names
span.quote: Excitatory synapses onto FS cells are typically strongly depressing. This includes thalamocortical inputs onto FS cells in layer IV and intracortical inputs onto FS cells in all layers. An exception to this is a population of FS neurons in layer VI that receives facilitating inputs, perhaps from corticothalamic neurons

span.label: VIP —part-of→ 5HT3aR
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — all VIP cells are in this group, and they are about 40 percent of it
span.quote: Lee et al. (2010) found that all VIP-expressing neurons in somatosensory cortex express 5HT3a receptors. Based on coexpression of VIP and EGFP in 5 Htr3aR-BAC EGFP mice, it was estimated that VIP-expressing neurons account for ~40% of the 5HT3aR population in S1

span.label: neurogliaform cells —part-of→ 5HT3aR
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the group is defined by three exclusions and one inclusion: reelin-positive, VIP-negative, SST-negative
span.quote: This reelin-positive, VIP-negative/SST-negative 5HT3aR group includes the neurogliaform cells.

span.label: calretinin —part-of→ SST
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.4 — the record marks this weak — A MARKER THAT CROSSES BOUNDARIES: about a third of SST cells carry it, and so do many VIP cells - which is why it cannot define a group
span.quote: For example, about a third of SST interneurons in frontal, somatosensory (S1), and visual cortex (V1) contain calretinin ( Xu et al., 2006 ). Some of this diversity within the SST population might be functionally significant. Although both SST/CR+ cells and SST/CR− cells exhibited similar Martinotti cell anatomical features and had similar adapting spike-firing patterns, they differed in the horizontal extension of their dendritic fields and number of primary processes

span.label: serotonin —causes→ 5HT3aR
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — and the response is universal within the group and absent in the other two, which is a functional check on a molecular definition
span.quote: Although 5HT3aR interneurons are heterogeneous, they are all potently modulated by ionotropic serotonin receptors ( Lee et al., 2010 ). Local somatic application of mCPBG, a 5HT3aR-selective agonist, to EGFP-positive neurons evoked fast and robust depolarization in more than 40 cells tested throughout all layers and including all the subtypes identified electrophysiologically. In contrast, no response was observed after application of mCPBG to PV and SST-expressing neurons.

span.label: reelin —part-of→ 5HT3aR
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: Non-VIP cells account for 60% of 5HT3aR neurons ( Lee et al., 2010 ). More than 80% of these interneurons expressed reelin, which is also expressed by a fraction of SST neurons but not by VIP 5HT3aR neurons ( Miyoshi et al., 2010 ). More than 90% of neurons in layer I belong to this group because only a small percentage of neurons in this layer expressed VIP.

span.label: Neurons expressing PV, SST or the 5HT3a receptor together account for nearly all GABAergic interneurons of primary somatosensory cortex, with the 5HT3aR group making up about 30%.
span.quote: This analysis revealed that 5HT3aR neurons account for ~30% of the total population of GABAergic neurons, and that three group of neurons, those expressing PV, SST, and 5HT3aR, account for nearly all, if not all, GABAergic interneurons in primary somatosensory cortex ( Fig. 1 ).

span.label: PV and SST proteins mark two non-overlapping interneuron populations, even though some PV cells carry SST mRNA.
span.quote: Thus, the data support the view that PV and SST protein expression defines two independent groups of GABAergic interneurons.

span.label: In layers I-III the 5HT3aR interneurons outnumber PV interneurons two to one, overturning the assumption that PV cells are the largest interneuron class there.
span.quote: Within layers I–III, the number of 5HT3aR-expressing neurons actually exceeds by two fold the number of PV-positive neurons, traditionally believed to represent the largest interneuron class.

span.label: Every VIP-expressing interneuron in somatosensory cortex also expresses the 5HT3a receptor, placing the whole VIP class inside the 5HT3aR group.

span.quote: Using the GENSAT line, Lee et al. (2010) found a nearly perfect overlap between EGFP and 5HT3a receptor mRNA expression in the neocortex. span.quote: Furthermore, it is likely that 5HT3aR mRNA expression reliably reports on the presence of functional receptors. Functional responses were detected to the specific 5HT3aR-agonist mCPBG in more than 40 EGFP-positive neurons recorded in the cortex of this transgenic line

span.label: neurons expressing PV, as detected by immunofluorescence, do not express SST protein and vice versa
span.quote: Our own studies in mouse have confirmed this conclusion; neurons expressing PV (as detected by immunofluorescence) do not express SST protein and vice versa

span.label: BUT BY mRNA THEY DO: under 10 percent of PV cells carry SST transcripts overall, 16.3 percent in layer VI, and a large percentage by RT-PCR of sorted cells
span.quote: We do find that using in situ hybridization (ISH) some PV-containing neurons (<10%) in somatosensory cortex contain SST mRNA. The overlap is largest in layer VI where ~16.3% of PV cells express SST mRNA ( Lee et al., 2010 ). Furthermore, RT-PCR of FACS purified PV-expressing neurons shows SST mRNA expression in a large percentage of the samples

span.label: and the conflict is settled by choosing protein as the definition, with the transcripts explained as levels too low to detect
span.quote: Together, the data suggest that although a fraction of PV neurons may express SST mRNA transcripts, SST protein levels are absent or are too low to be detected by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Thus, the data support the view that PV and SST protein expression defines two independent groups of GABAergic interneurons.

span.label: A CATEGORY THAT NEEDED A TOOL TO EXIST: there are no antibodies to the 5HT3a receptor, so this population could not be counted until a reporter line was made

span.label: before that, its size was a qualitative impression from fluorescence

span.label: ONE CELL TYPE, FOUR NAMES IN ONE SENTENCE: burst spiking nonpyramidal, intrinsic bursting and low-threshold spike all name the regular adapting Martinotti cells
span.quote: They display a regular adapting firing pattern (RSNP), but often, particularly in layer V, they initially fire bursts of two or more spikes on slow depolarizing humps when depolarized from hyperpolarized potentials (because of this property, these cells have also been called burst spiking nonpyramidal (BSNP), intrinsic bursting (IB), or low-threshold spike (LTS) cells).

span.label: AND THREE MORE FOR ANOTHER: rapid-adapting, fast-adapting and IS2 name the same VIP subtype
span.quote: These cells have been named rapid-adapting ( Butt et al., 2005 ), fast-adapting ( Lee et al., 2010 ; Miyoshi et al., 2010 ), and IS2 ( Porter et al., 1998 ) and seem to be the major VIP subtype that does not coexpress CR.

span.label: LS1 cells correspond to neurogliaform cells, whereas LS2 cells have larger somata and longer, less branching dendrites
span.quote: LS1 cells correspond to neurogliaform cells, whereas LS2 cells exhibit larger soma size and longer but less branching dendrites

span.label: A CLASS REPORTED ONCE AND NOT REPLICATED: the preponderance of this class of PV neurons is not known and it has not been described by other investigators
span.quote: The preponderance of this class of PV neurons is not known and has not been described by other investigators; perhaps because Blatow et al. used 14-day-old mice, somewhat younger than what is typically used in the field and carried their recordings at room temperature.

span.label: with two specific methodological differences offered as the reason: 14-day-old mice and room-temperature recording
span.quote: The preponderance of this class of PV neurons is not known and has not been described by other investigators; perhaps because Blatow et al. used 14-day-old mice, somewhat younger than what is typically used in the field and carried their recordings at room temperature.

( Ma et al., 2006 ; Xu et al., 2006 ; Fanselow et al., 2008 ; Xu and Callaway, 2009 ). McGarry et al. (2010) used mice with an average age of P14 (range P10–18), which is younger than what other investigators have used. span.label: THE CORRESPONDENCE PROBLEM STATED OUTRIGHT: subtypes described by different investigators cannot easily be matched to one another, which calls for better classification tools

span.label: virtually all parvalbumin cells recorded across several mouse lines were fast-spiking
span.quote: PV expression has been associated with the fast-spiking firing pattern since the 1980s ( Kawaguchi et al., 1987 ). We have recorded from several hundred PV-expressing neurons in several mouse lines expressing GFP in PV neurons and virtually all are fast-spiking.

span.label: fast-spiking cells have the lowest input resistance and fastest membrane time constant of all interneurons
span.quote: FS cells fire sustained high-frequency trains of brief APs with a large and fast AHP and with little spike frequency adaptation. Near threshold, they fire abrupt episodes of nonadapting repetitive discharges. They have the lowest input resistance and the fastest membrane time constant of all interneurons, a feature that contributes to ensure fast synaptic responses

span.label: excitatory synapses onto fast-spiking cells depress, with one layer VI exception that facilitates

span.label: excitatory inputs onto Martinotti cells facilitate instead, which is called the key feature distinguishing them from fast-spiking cells
span.quote: Excitatory inputs onto Martinotti cells are generally strongly facilitating, which is a key feature that distinguishes these interneurons from FS neurons

span.label: so a single pyramidal cell firing repetitively can drive a Martinotti cell and produce feedback inhibition across layers and columns
span.quote: As a result of this feature, repetitive activity in a single pyramidal cell can drive a Martinotti cell to fire and provide feedback inhibition to pyramidal neurons across layers and columns

span.label: chandelier cell function is contested, with their GABA release possibly depolarising and even excitatory at the axon initial segment

span.label: and 5HT3aR cells are also excited by cholinergic agonists acting on nicotinic receptors, a common property independently of layer location or electrophysiological or morphological subtype
span.quote: Interestingly, 5HT3aR are also excited by cholinergic agonists acting on nicotinic receptors. This also seems to be a common property of all 5HT3aR neurons independently of layer location or electrophysiological or morphological subtype

(2010) demonstrate that FS versus non-FS GABAergic interneurons in superficial layers are differentially modulated depending on the brain state and behavioral context of the animal ( Gentet et al., 2010 ). By recording intracellularly using GAD67-GFP mice, Gentet et al. showed that non-FS INs become more depolarized and exhibit enhanced firing rates during whisking periods, which presumably corresponds to an alert state. To our knowledge, this study provides the first direct evidence that different types of interneurons might be recruited differentially depending on a brain state and behavioral context of awake animals. Gentet et al. did not determine which types of non-FS interneurons were engaged during whisking; however, given their abundance relative to SST interneurons in superficial layers, it is likely that these were 5HT3aR neurons.
